expectations.text: The report raises a finding that hold allocation's scanning-branch-first rule (a returned copy goes to the oldest hold at the branch where it was scanned before any other branch) works against the HLD tenet 'Waiting is honored in sequence', grounded in a title with holds at more than one branch, where a patron who asked later at the scanning branch receives a copy ahead of one who asked earlier elsewhere. A finding that only notes the missing Decisions row, without the tenet, does not pass.
expectations.evidence: finding ties branch-first allocation to 'Waiting is honored in sequence'

expectations.text: The report does not flag the pickup-notices design, or any other mechanism besides the branch-first allocation rule, as working against an HLD tenet or goal.
expectations.evidence: no other mechanism flagged against a tenet/goal
